issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of a pipeline right of user takes only a limited facet of property rights and does not amount to acquisition of the land or its entire proprietary interest.
material_facts: The notified parcels were recorded as agricultural land when the acquisition process began.

The pipeline was laid underground, and the owners and occupiers retained title, possession, and the ability to use the land for its prior purposes, subject to restrictions on construction, excavation, and planting trees.
The statutory scheme prohibited laying pipelines beneath residential-use land, land with an existing permanent structure, and land appurtenant to a dwelling house.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was of the limited right to use the sub-soil for laying and maintaining pipelines, not of the land itself or the owners’ entire proprietary interest.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the acquisition and use provisions of Sections 7 and 9 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, and the understanding of property as an aggregate of rights stated in Jilubhai Nanbhai Khachar v. State of Gujarat. The acquisition of one facet of property rights does not itself amount to acquisition of all ownership or possessory rights.

predicates.pipeline_right_of_user_acquisition: The proceeding concerns acquisition of a right to use land for an underground pipeline.
predicates.land_remains_in_owner_possession: The landowner or occupier retains possession of the land after the pipeline right is acquired.
predicates.prior_land_use_remains_permitted: The owner or occupier remains entitled to use the land for the purpose for which it was used before the acquisition, subject to specified safeguards for the pipeline.

issues.definition: When a pipeline right-of-user proceeding leaves possession and the permitted prior use with the owner or occupier, the acquired interest is only the limited pipeline user right.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory principles for compensating acquisition of a pipeline right of user and resulting damage, loss, or injury are not invalid or illusory, and the compensation in this case was not inadequate.
material_facts: The compensation scheme provided compensation for actual damage, loss, or injury caused by entry, pipeline-laying, or later pipeline work, separately from compensation for acquisition of the right of user calculated by reference to the land’s market value.
The owners and occupiers retained title and possession, although their use of the land was restricted in order to protect the pipeline.
The parcels were agricultural land when the initial notification was issued; permissions to convert some parcels to non-agricultural use were granted afterward.
Compensation was agreed at rates above the average recorded sale rate, and provisional compensation at a higher rate was deposited while the proceedings were pending.
issues.conclusion: The compensation provisions were not invalid or illusory, and the compensation on the record could not be called inadequate.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, compensation for actual damage, loss, or injury is distinct from additional compensation for the acquired right of user, calculated by reference to market value. Section 10(3) requires regard to specified forms of loss, including injury to property or earnings. The Court held that permanent impairment may support compensation and distinguished H.D. Vora v. State of Maharashtra, finding its principle inapplicable. It also relied on the Statement of Objects and Reasons and the separate compensation elements in Section 10.

predicates.pipeline_right_of_user_acquisition: The proceeding concerns acquisition of a limited right to use land for a pipeline.
predicates.actual_loss_is_separately_compensable: The scheme provides compensation for damage, loss, or injury caused by pipeline-related activities apart from compensation for the acquired user right.
predicates.additional_compensation_reflects_land_va: The scheme provides additional compensation for the user right by reference to the land’s market value.
predicates.ownership_and_possession_remain: The landowner or occupier retains title and possession despite the pipeline right being acquired.

issues.definition: Where a pipeline acquisition leaves ownership and possession with the owner and provides distinct compensation for actual loss and for the acquired user right by reference to land value, the compensation scheme is not illusory.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory definition of a corporation broad enough to include companies permits a private-sector company to acquire a pipeline right of user for an activity serving the public interest.
material_facts: The pipeline was designed to transport natural gas over a long distance and to serve consumers.
The pipeline activity was subject to statutory regulation and was undertaken through a private-sector company.
The statutory definition of corporation included companies formed and registered under company law.
issues.conclusion: The statutory definition of corporation includes private-sector entities, and there was no basis to restrict it to public-sector corporations.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the definition of corporation in Section 2(b) of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962. It considered the public importance and statutory regulation of natural-gas transportation and held that the definition was intentionally broad enough to encompass private-sector entities.

predicates.pipeline_right_of_user_acquisition: The proceeding concerns acquisition of a right to use land for laying a pipeline.
predicates.private_entity_is_a_company: The entity seeking the pipeline right is a company formed and registered under applicable company law.
predicates.pipeline_activity_serves_public_interest: The pipeline activity is directed to meeting public needs and is subject to statutory regulation.

issues.definition: A private company may qualify as the holder of a pipeline right when the pipeline acquisition serves a public-interest activity.

issues.legal_issue: A person appointed to determine objections and compensation as the competent authority must have judicial-office experience at least equivalent to that of a Subordinate Judge or be a trained legal mind.
material_facts: The competent authority had powers to hear and decide objections, report recommendations to the government, determine compensation for damage or loss, and assess the land’s market value.
The governing statute and its rules did not specify qualifications or a transparent appointment process for the competent authority.
A comparable enactment required its competent authority to hold or have held judicial office at least at the level of a Subordinate Judge.
The appointment qualification defect was considered in proceedings challenging acquisition and related statutory arrangements.
issues.conclusion: To satisfy fairness under Article 14 of the Constitution, the competent authority must hold or have held judicial office not lower in rank than a Subordinate Judge or be a trained legal mind; actions already taken are not invalidated solely on this ground.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Article 14 of the Constitution, considered the quasi-judicial functions and civil-rights consequences of the competent authority’s decisions, and relied on the qualification provision in Section 16(2) of the Metro Railway (Construction of Works) Act, 1978, as a comparable enactment. It also relied on the observations in Trilok Sudhirbhai Pandya v. Union of India concerning the authority’s wide powers and the need to guard against bias. The Court stated that past actions would not be impaired or invalidated purely for lack of the specified qualification.

predicates.pipeline_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns acquisition of a right to use land for a pipeline.
predicates.competent_authority_exercises_quasi_judi: The appointed authority decides objections or compensation matters affecting the civil rights of persons interested in the land.

issues.definition: In a pipeline acquisition proceeding, an authority exercising quasi-judicial powers must have the specified judicial experience or be a trained legal mind.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of a fixed statutory deadline for determining and depositing compensation does not invalidate the compensation scheme, although compensation is expected to be determined and deposited within a reasonable time.
material_facts: The statute and rules did not fix a period for determining or depositing compensation for damage, loss, or injury or for acquisition of the right of user.
Most of the compensation assessed in the first instance in this case had been deposited in advance.
Damage caused by initial entry or pipeline laying could be one-time, while damage caused by later maintenance entries could recur.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a prescribed deadline did not invalidate the scheme; the authorities are expected to determine and deposit compensation within a reasonable time.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the compensation scheme under Section 10 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, and held that the absence of a statutory time limit did not, by itself, render the scheme invalid. It stated that authorities should act within a reasonable time, taking account of the possibility that compensation-related damage may recur during maintenance.

predicates.pipeline_right_of_user_acquisition: The proceeding concerns acquisition of a right to use land for a pipeline.
predicates.compensation_law_sets_no_fixed_deadline: The applicable compensation scheme does not prescribe a time limit for determining or depositing compensation.

issues.definition: When a pipeline user-right proceeding has no fixed compensation deadline, the authorities are expected to determine and deposit compensation within a reasonable time.

issues.legal_issue: A special law allowing acquisition of a pipeline right of user does not exclude acquisition of the land itself under the general land-acquisition law when the circumstances require it.
material_facts: The pipeline legislation provided for acquisition of a limited right of user rather than outright acquisition of the land.
The legislation expressly stated that its provisions were additional to, and not in derogation of, other laws relating to land acquisition.
The Court identified possible pipeline-related needs, such as permanent monitoring or flow-control facilities, that could require acquisition of land rather than only a sub-soil user right.
issues.conclusion: The general land-acquisition law may still be used where the circumstances and needs require acquisition of the land itself.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 18 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962, which makes that Act additional to, and not in derogation of, other laws relating to land acquisition. The limited user-right mechanism does not bar resort to general acquisition law when outright acquisition is required.

predicates.pipeline_infrastructure_proceeding: The proceeding concerns land needed for pipeline infrastructure.
predicates.permanent_facilities_require_land_acquis: Permanent monitoring, flow-control, or comparable facilities require the land itself rather than only a right to use its sub-soil.
predicates.limited_user_right_is_insufficient: The limited pipeline user right would not meet the land requirement in the circumstances.

issues.definition: For pipeline infrastructure, general land acquisition remains available when permanent facilities or other circumstances require more than the limited user right.
